# 🤖 Claude Code Review — [cli/cli#13469](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/13469)
> _Improve update --all command if some skills don't have metadata_ · by @tommaso-moro · 2 files (+39 / -2)

## 📋 Summary
This PR fixes `gh skill update --all` so that skills lacking GitHub metadata are skipped with a notice instead of triggering an interactive prompt, aligning the command with the "without prompting" semantics of `--all`. It also clarifies the warning message to tell users how to add metadata (run `gh skill update <skill>` interactively or reinstall) and adds a regression test.

## ⚠️ Risks
- The core change in `updateRun` (`update.go`) — `if !canPrompt || opts.All` — is the only behavioral guard shown. The diff is partial: we cannot see how `canPrompt`, `opts.All`, the `updates` slice, or the final exit logic are constructed, so I'm inferring (from the visible `continue`) that no-metadata skills are correctly excluded from `updates`. If `opts.All` interacts with another prompt path not shown in these two hunks, that path would not be covered.
- The updated warning string in `update.go` advises users to "Run `gh skill update manual-skill` interactively to add metadata," but running that command in a non-interactive environment (`!canPrompt`) would itself skip rather than prompt. The guidance is only accurate in a TTY, which could mislead CI/non-interactive users who hit the same notice.
- The new test (`update_test.go`, "all skips no-metadata skill without prompting") only asserts a substring of stderr. It does not assert the skill was *not* updated, that no HTTP calls were made, or the command's exit/result, so a regression that prompts-and-also-updates could still pass as long as the stderr text appears.

## 💡 Suggestions
- In `update_test.go`, strengthen the assertion: confirm `updates` is empty / no update occurred and that the empty `stubs` registry received no requests, in addition to the stderr substring — this guards the "skipped, not updated" invariant, not just the message text.
- Consider conditioning the "Run `gh skill update <skill>` interactively to add metadata" half of the message on `canPrompt`, so non-interactive runs don't get advice that won't work in their context.
- The skill name is interpolated into a backtick-quoted shell command in the warning (`gh skill update %s`). If skill names can contain spaces or shell-significant characters, the suggested command would be malformed; a brief note or quoting could help (low priority if names are validated elsewhere — not visible in the diff).

## 🎯 Confidence
**High** — the change is small, self-contained, and the producer (`noMeta` append) and consumer (the warning loop) are both visible; the main caveat is that the surrounding `updateRun` logic isn't fully shown.
